preconditions.description: The number of elements in the given array is between 2 and 100000, inclusive.
The number of elements that can be changed is between 0 and the minimum of 10 or N-2, inclusive.
Each element in the given array is between -10^9 and 10^9, inclusive.

postconditions.description: The output array has the same number of elements as the input array.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i+1] - output[i] == output[i] - output[i-1] for i in range(1, N-1) if output[i] != -1)
postconditions.description: The output array is an arithmetic progression with at most K changes.

postconditions.expression: sum(1 for i in range(N) if output[i] == -1) <= K
postconditions.description: The number of elements that were changed is at most K.

postconditions.expression: not any(output[i] != -1 and output[i+1] != -1 and (output[i] - output[i-1]) != (output[i+1] - output[i]) for i in range(1, N-1))
postconditions.description: The output array is the most beautiful arithmetic progression, as defined in the problem statement.
